title: Plan last-mile solar sales in Nankanga
skills_assessed: Data-informed planning with spreadsheets and maps

role.title: Field sales manager
role.company_context: Off-grid solar distributor expanding last-mile retail of portable solar lanterns across rural Tanzania. Regional sales managers own territory P&L, agent networks, inventory movement from regional hubs, and field reporting quality. Hiring for Mbeya to turn a defined community target into a credible six-month operating plan.
day_to_day: Set weekly unit and cash targets for village agents and team leads
Plan inventory pulls from the Mbeya hub and last-mile transport into communities
Hire, train, and coach agents on product demos, pricing, and cash handling
Review agent sales logs for anomalies, stockouts, and suspected fraud
Report progress to regional leadership with simple tools (spreadsheets, maps, short written updates)
required_skills: Can build a coherent sales plan that ties headcount, pay, inventory, and transport to a unit target and budget
Comfortable using spreadsheet data and basic map/GPS context for territory decisions
Can describe practical fraud controls for cash and inventory in the field
Can specify how field staff report activity without inventing heavy enterprise software
nice_to_have_skills: Prior last-mile, FMCG, or PAYG solar field experience in East Africa
Familiarity with QGIS or similar for plotting community points
Experience designing agent commission and training curricula
constraints: Assessment is a planning and talk-through exercise using provided desktop data — not building production software or a full CRM
Do not require cloud SaaS accounts or paid datasets beyond what is on the desktop
Candidates may use browser, spreadsheets, and QGIS; starter CSVs on the desktop are shared scenery, not a solved plan
Do not turn the challenge into a pure math puzzle with one correct org chart

problem_statement.title: Sell 500 Sunking Pico Plus units in Nankanga
problem_statement.summary: You are a sales manager covering the Mbeya region, Tanzania. You have a $10,000 budget to sell 500 units of the Sunking Pico Plus in six months in the Nankanga community (GPS: -8.255937980286378, 32.05191394550532). Starter CSVs on the desktop give community, product, transport, labor, sample sales, and map context — use them. Write a thorough plan covering as many operating aspects as you can; the more complete and spoken-through your reasoning, the stronger the result.
outcomes: Produce a written operating plan for hitting the unit target within budget and timeline.
Address hiring (how many people, pay, training), logistics into the community, how units/connections are sold, fraud mitigation, and how sales managers/agents report back.
Ground the plan in the provided CSVs and, where useful, spreadsheets or QGIS on the desktop.
constraints: Stay within the stated budget, unit target, product, community, and six-month window unless you explicitly justify a trade-off.
Do not invent a different product line or geography as the primary plan.
Prefer concrete numbers (headcount, pay, trips, stock) over slogans; show how they fit the budget.
Talk through your reasoning in depth — sparse bullet lists without justification are weak.
problem_statement.deliverables: A clear written plan (document or long-form notes) that a reviewer can follow: team design, economics, logistics, selling approach, fraud controls, and reporting tools. Optionally include spreadsheet working files or map screenshots that support the numbers — not required if the written plan is complete and consistent with the data.

rubric.name: Feasibility and unit economics
rubric.description: YES/NO: Are budget and unit math coherent for the stated unit target in six months, with inventory, pay, and transport costs plausible relative to the provided rate cards? Answer YES only if the numbers add up against the starter CSVs and stay within (or explicitly justify trade-offs on) the stated budget / unit-target frame from the brief. Incoherent totals, ignored budget/target, or rates that contradict the data = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Go-to-market and logistics
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the plan describe a credible path from the Mbeya hub to the stated target community and a selling motion suited to that community (agents, market days, demos) rather than generic marketing copy? Answer YES only if both logistics into the community and a grounded selling approach are present. Generic sales theory with no last-mile path, or logistics with no selling motion = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Team and operations design
rubric.description: YES/NO: Are hiring, pay, training, and span of control specific and operable, with roles matching the labor_rates context? Answer YES only if headcount/pay/training are concrete enough to run and consistent with the provided labor data. Vague org slogans or pay/roles that ignore labor_rates = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Fraud and reporting controls
rubric.description: YES/NO: Does the plan name practical fraud risks (cash, phantom sales, stock leakage) and simple reporting tools field staff can actually use? Answer YES only if both fraud controls and a usable reporting approach are present. Missing fraud discussion, or inventing heavy enterprise software with no practical field reporting = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.

rubric.name: Clarity and use of data
rubric.description: YES/NO: Is the plan thorough and well reasoned, and does it reference starter CSVs/maps where relevant instead of ignoring them? Answer YES if depth of reasoning is clear and the provided data is used. Extremely sparse bullets without justification, or a plan that never engages the starter files = NO. YES = full points; NO or unclear = 0.
